## What's changed

OpenCode becomes a full coding agent in workflows: save an OpenCode API key, pick a model and effort on an agent profile, and choose the model from a fetched list. This release also brings passkey sign-in, an MCP server for Kuayle and wiki page references.

### OpenCode in agent profiles and workflows

- **OpenCode API key.** Each user can save an OpenCode API key in the agent sign-in settings, next to the Claude Code token. It is stored encrypted, never returned, and passed to that user's OpenCode runs as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. (#206, KUA-117)
- **Model and effort.** An OpenCode profile or task can set a model in `provider/model` form, for example `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and an effort. Kuayle passes them to `opencode run` as `--model` and `--variant`. OpenCode never runs on a workspace model server. (#207, KUA-118)
- **Model suggestions.** The model field of an agent profile, the task composer and the approval card suggest the models of the OpenCode Go plan, read from OpenCode's public model list, and limit the effort to the levels the chosen model allows. Typing any other model still works. Claude Code and Codex profiles suggest the models of the workspace's model servers. (#208, KUA-119)
- **Unusable profiles are refused when saved.** A profile whose coding agent cannot run with its model or effort is rejected with the reason, and a workflow with such a step cannot be saved or set as a default. When a task still cannot start, the approval card names the workflow, the step and the profile instead of "The coding task request was rejected". (#204, KUA-116)

### Also in this release

- Passkey (WebAuthn) sign-in and passkey management. (#198, KUA-114)
- An MCP server for Kuayle. (#188, KUA-101)
- Wiki pages can be referenced from issues, comments and other wiki pages, with @ mentions and drag and drop. (#193, KUA-98)
- The GitHub bot's picture appears in PR descriptions, with the Kuayle logo for the GitHub App. (#192, KUA-112)
- A failed task keeps the workflow's reason. (#202, KUA-120)
- A weekly usage limit message's reset date is read correctly. (#201, KUA-113)
- Drag an issue to another group in cycle and project lists, and empty statuses show as drop targets when grouped by status. Thanks @kasperhartwich. (#199, #200)

### Upgrade notes

- Migrations `000138_passkeys`, `000139_issue_wiki_references`, `000140_wiki_page_mentions` and `000141_opencode_api_key` run on upgrade. No action is needed.
- The server reads OpenCode's model list from `opencode.ai`. If outbound access is blocked, the model field still accepts typed input and saving is not blocked. With an explicit `DEV_MACHINE_EGRESS_ALLOWLIST`, add `opencode.ai` so OpenCode runs can reach their provider.
- Existing profiles that no longer pass the new checks keep loading and running as before; the checks apply the next time they are saved.

### Known limits

- Kuayle does not verify an OpenCode API key when it is saved; a wrong key shows as the agent's own error in the run.
- Model suggestions for OpenCode cover the OpenCode Go plan only. Models of other OpenCode providers are typed by hand.

## What's changed

Agent tasks now survive the provider's usage limit. When Claude Code hits its 5-hour or weekly limit (or Codex its usage limit), the task is paused instead of failed, and it continues by itself after the limit resets.

### Agent tasks

- A task whose agent hits the provider's usage limit is **paused**, not failed. It keeps its worktree and the agent's session. (#195, KUA-113)
- The task card shows the provider's message, when the limit resets, and when the task resumes, with **Resume now** and **Don't resume**. The transcript says "Paused at the usage limit" instead of "Stopped with an error".
- After the reset the task **resumes automatically** on the same session, at most five times in a row; after that you resume it.
- While your own agent subscription is limited, your other queued tasks for that agent wait for the reset instead of starting and failing. Tasks that use a workspace model server are not held.
- A limit message Kuayle does not recognise still fails the task as before.

### Upgrade notes

- Migration `000137_agent_task_usage_limits` runs on upgrade. It adds columns to `agent_tasks` and one small table; no action is needed.
- Tasks that failed at a usage limit before this release stay failed. Retry them as usual.

## What's changed

A second security release. It completes three fixes from the November 2026 audit that v0.2.25 had only partly delivered; `SECURITY_AUDIT.md` records them. Read the upgrade notes first: one change needs an action from operators who never set a database password.

### Security

- Task previews run in their own container. A preview no longer runs in the developer container next to its secrets, agent sign-ins and sudo; it gets the same isolation as an agent run, and reviewers open it the same way as before. (#196)
- Remote images in issues, comments, wiki pages and public links load only when the reader asks. Content shows a placeholder naming the host, with "Load image" and "Always load from this host". Uploaded images are not affected. (#197)
- Outside development, the server and `update.sh` also refuse the database password the Compose files fall back to when `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is not set. (#194)

### Upgrade notes

- **If your `.env` has no `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` line, change the database password before upgrading.** Without one, the Compose files use a password that is published in the repository. After this update the backend does not start with it and `update.sh` refuses to update, naming the setting. "Secrets must be generated" in `docs/self-hosting.md` explains how to change the password of a running database. The notes of v0.2.25 about placeholder secrets and the GitHub App permission still apply if you are upgrading from an older version.
- **Task previews**: a preview started before the upgrade keeps running where it is until it is stopped or started again. From the developer terminal a preview is no longer on `localhost`; it has its own address on the machine network (see the previews section of `BE/docs/agent-tasks.md`).
- Migration 000136: a new routing target for preview containers. The machine gateway's database role needs no new grant.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.25...v0.2.26

## What's changed

This is mainly a security release. It fixes the findings of the November 2026 audit, recorded in `SECURITY_AUDIT.md`. Upgrading is recommended. Read the upgrade notes first: two changes need an action from operators.

### New

- Copy any chat message, including a coding agent's messages, with one click. (#185)
- A public OpenAPI reference for the HTTP API: the server publishes it at `/api/openapi.json`, and the website has an API reference page. It covers the routes a personal access token can use. (#186)

### Security

- Workspace import now sanitizes rich text the same way the editor does, and the app no longer parses stored content as live HTML when it only needs the text. (#175)
- Publishing an agent's work no longer loads the git configuration of the task checkout, which agents can write. (#173)
- Task previews start only when the task's creator asks, not automatically when a task reaches review. (#172)
- Public share links search only what the share shows, and filters added by a viewer can only narrow what the share was created with. (#176)
- Only the task creator's own comment starts a follow-up run. Comments by other members are recorded for the creator to act on. (#177)
- When the assistant wants to message a running coding agent, it now asks for your approval and shows the exact text first. (#182)
- The server refuses to start outside development while a secret is still an example placeholder or a development default. (#178)
- Invite links stop working when their creator is removed or loses the right to invite. A password reset also revokes personal access tokens. Creating, editing and deleting saved views needs the `view:manage` permission, which guests do not have. (#181)
- In public demo mode, the rule that only system administrators use Dev Machines is enforced for every way work can start on a machine. (#189)
- Connecting a shared GitHub App installation requires the account it is installed on, or an owner of that organization. (#180)
- Content keeps only the CSS classes the editor produces, and issue template descriptions are sanitized like issue descriptions. (#187)
- GitHub webhook deliveries are processed once. Mention reviews and review feedback are accepted only from people GitHub confirms can write to the repository. (#190)
- The release process pins agent CLIs only to versions published at least 48 hours ago. (#184)
- `.env.*` files are ignored by git, except the examples. (#183)

### Upgrade notes

- **Replace placeholder secrets before upgrading.** If your `.env` still holds a `CHANGE_ME_…` value or a development default for `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, the gateway database password or another secret, the backend will not start after this update and its log names the setting. Generate real values first (`openssl rand -hex 32`); "Secrets must be generated" in `docs/self-hosting.md` explains how, including how to change the database password of an existing installation. The first update to this version still runs the previous `update.sh`, which does not check this for you.
- **Shared GitHub App: add the organization permission "Members: Read-only".** Until it is added and each organization accepts it, new organization installations cannot be connected. Existing connections and installations on personal accounts are not affected. Workspaces that use their own GitHub App need no change.
- **Task previews** no longer start by themselves; start them from the task.
- **Comment follow-ups**: a comment by someone other than the task's creator no longer starts a run.
- **Personal access tokens** are revoked by a password reset; create new ones afterwards.
- **Guests** can no longer create, edit or delete saved views.
- **Git filters defined only in a repository's local configuration** (for example Git LFS installed with `--local`) are not applied when Kuayle publishes a task; such files are committed as they are in the working tree.
- Migrations 000134 and 000135: approvals for messages to a coding agent, and the record of processed GitHub webhook deliveries.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.24...v0.2.25

## What's changed

### Wiki
- Teams and projects each get a wiki: Markdown pages in a page tree with folders, autosave, history with git-style diffs, and live updates. Access follows the owning team or project. (#161)
- Publish a page inside the workspace or by public link. Pages can be moved between folders.
- An opt-in daily registry per wiki: agents log their work there, with AI overviews on demand or on a schedule.
- The assistant can read, write, move, publish and share wiki pages. Destructive actions ask for approval first.

### Teams and projects
- Change a team's key (the `ENG` in `ENG-12`). Every issue identifier is updated, and the old key keeps working, so old links, branches and PRs still resolve. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#160)
- Use an uploaded image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or ICO, up to 1 MB) as a team's icon. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#158)
- Projects get a colour and an icon, shown in the sidebar, on issue rows, board cards and the issue header. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#157)
- Rename a project inline from its page. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#155)

### Issues
- Bulk "Set project": move many selected issues to a project, or remove their project, in one step. It never overwrites edits other people make at the same time. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#159)
- With a custom workflow group order, the first page of the issue list now shows the groups in the right order. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#154)

### Everywhere
- Every page has its own browser tab title, page name first, e.g. "Labels < Settings < Kuayle". Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#156)

### Fixes
- Bulk "set parent" no longer overwrites edits other people make at the same time, and refuses a change that would create a loop, writing nothing. (#163)
- Deleting a workspace while someone uploaded a team icon could deadlock. (#164)

### Upgrade notes
- Migrations 000124 to 000133: wiki pages, versions, registry, overviews, approvals, page tree, publishing and share approvals, then project colour and icon, then team key aliases.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.23...v0.2.24

## What's changed

### Workflows
- A new workflow editor that fills the page. Edit on the canvas with right-click menus, a + under each step to add the next one, drag to connect, and a floating toolbar with undo/redo, tidy up and zoom. The side panel has Inspect, Outline and Settings tabs.
- Edit the built-in Standard workflow. Your copy runs wherever Standard applies, and you can restore the built-in one at any time. Workflows can now be deleted rather than archived.
- New "Full cycle" template that uses every kind of step. Every failure and every request for changes goes back to the implementer, up to 5 times, then asks you.
- "Automated review" block, and "Retry on failure" for agent and publish steps.
- Loops back to earlier steps each get their own line, so they no longer overlap. Leaving with unsaved changes asks in a dialog.
- Retrying a failed workflow task keeps the instructions of the step it reruns.

### Agents
- Agent profiles open in a side panel with Markdown instructions (up to 64 KB) and skills from the workspace library. When a workflow step runs, Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode receive the profile's instructions and skills as files (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md and SKILL.md).
- Ask AI in the skill, instructions and step prompt editors: write the whole text, or rewrite only the selection, with undo. It uses the model from Settings → AI.
- Wizards for new skills and new custom tools, drafted with AI and reviewed before saving. AI never sets a tool's run mode or keeps credentials.
- Follow-ups after an agent review include all of its findings, and a request for changes that a later approval superseded is no longer sent back. (#152)

### Assistant
- A calmer coding task card: one row of actions, everything else in a menu, and an inline reply box.
- Approval requests now always appear after the assistant's reply.

### Settings
- Version page: System update sits above the changelog, and release dates appear next to versions. Thanks @kasperhartwich! (#153)
- Shorter labels across workflows, agents and AI editing in all four languages.

### Upgrade notes
- Migrations 000120 to 000123: edited Standard workflows, 64 KB profile instructions, profile skills, and profile files recorded on agent runs.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.22...v0.2.23

## What's changed

### Customizable GitHub bot
- **Settings → GitHub → Kuayle bot** sets the bot's display name and profile picture. You can upload a PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF up to 2 MB, or link one from an https:// address. Kuayle starts each GitHub comment with this name and picture. GitHub still shows the GitHub App as the author. (#145)
- Each workspace can turn the bot's abilities on or off: linking issues, task feedback from CI and change requests, posting review findings, pull request actions, merging, releases. A disabled ability is refused wherever the GitHub write happens, whoever asked for it. Existing abilities stay on by default. (#145)
- New, off by default: the bot can start an agent review when a trusted commenter mentions it on a pull request and asks for one. You can choose the harness and model it uses. (#145)
- Migration 000119 adds the per-workspace bot settings table. (#145)

### For contributors
- New `kuayle-review` agent skill for peer reviews of a PR, one area or the whole codebase. It covers security, correctness, architecture flows, maintainability, UI, UX, performance, tests and operations, with a severity rubric and a report format. (#149)

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.21...v0.2.22

## What's changed

### Configurable workflows
- Design your own development flows as editable state machines in **Settings → Workflows**: agent steps, checks/CI, approvals, publish, merge and end nodes, with conditions on each transition, loop guards and a per-task budget. Workflows are versioned, validated before saving (unreachable nodes, unguarded loops and missing profiles are refused), and can be set as the default per workspace, project or team, or picked per task. (#146)
- **Agent profiles** in Settings → Agents: reusable agents with a role, harness, model, effort and instructions. Built-in Implementer and Reviewer profiles. Profiles can't widen workspace policy. (#146)
- The task's Agents panel shows the workflow graph, the current node, the path taken and why each transition fired. The fixed flow is now the built-in "Standard" workflow, so nothing changes until you pick another. (#146)

### Dev machines
- A task machine can now run up to **10 tasks** (default 10 for new workspaces; saved values are kept), set with a slider. Each agent's memory limit is split across the tasks running on the machine, so tasks slow down instead of being killed. (#147)
- The Merge method card now sits above the policy's Save button and is more compact. (#147)

### Fixes
- The workflows migration is renumbered to 000118 so it no longer clashes with the tasks-per-machine migration, and a test now catches duplicate migration versions. (#150)

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.20...v0.2.21

## What's changed

### Agent reviews reach the follow-up in full
- When you approve a follow-up in the assistant after an agent review asked for changes, Kuayle now attaches **every finding** of that review (the latest finished review of the published commit) to the follow-up, instead of relying on the assistant's summary. Coding agents can't read Kuayle's reviews, so before this they could miss findings or stop to ask for them. Reviews of older commits, approvals and unfinished reviews are not attached. (#148)
- Agent run summaries are now kept up to 16 KiB instead of 4000 bytes, cut on a character boundary, so long reviewer findings are no longer truncated mid-sentence. (#148)

### For contributors
- The agent harness now says to access the web with headless Playwright, never a browser extension. (#148)

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/carbogninalberto/kuayle/compare/v0.2.19...v0.2.20

### Fixed
- **Agent tasks no longer fail on a short database slowdown.** A slow database write used to stop the agent run after 5 seconds, losing up to an hour of work. Kuayle now retries the write for up to three minutes. If a failed run's container won't stop, it's killed instead of left running.
- **Task attempts get three hours instead of one.** Large issues often need longer than an hour to build and test.
- **Machine usage charts keep updating while agents run.** Sampling could stop for the whole run when a Docker call stalled. Each machine's check now has a time limit, and it no longer holds up other machine work.
- **The CPU chart shows real usage.** It read 0% on every machine before.

### Improvements
- **Far fewer file events.** Machines no longer record an event for every file in build output, caches, `node_modules` or agent scratch folders. When many files change at once, for example after a checkout or an install, one summary event replaces thousands. Busy machines wrote about 20 events a second before. Existing machines get the new collector when they're next idle, or when they're started from stopped.

### Features
- **Machines share their CPU and memory.** A 16 GB, 16 CPU machine now gives a build all of its 16 GB and 16 CPUs, not one container's fixed share. Previously the Docker daemon got 40% and the agent and terminal 35% each.
  - **How:** on hosts where Docker uses systemd with cgroup v2, each new machine's containers run in one systemd slice. The slice is capped at the machine's memory and CPUs, with swap up to `DEV_MACHINE_SWAP_PERCENT` of its memory (default 50).
  - **Infrastructure:** the collector and egress proxy keep their small limits, so a runaway build can't starve them.
  - **Clearer alerts:** an out-of-memory alert names the machine's limit: "the machine reached its 16 GiB memory limit and a process in the Docker daemon container was stopped".
  - **Lifecycle:** limits survive host reboots, resizing updates them, and teardown removes them.
  - **The manager stays unprivileged.** Each change runs in a short-lived, capability-free helper container that only reaches systemd.
  - **Which machines:** existing machines keep the old shares until they're recreated. Docker Desktop and other non-systemd hosts keep them too. `DEV_MACHINE_SLICES=off` turns sharing off.
- **A redesigned machine page.**
  - **Layout:** a header with status and actions, then a summary of size, repository, creation and last activity. Below that are tabs: **Overview**, **Worktrees & tasks**, **Apps & services** and **Activity**.
  - **Usage charts:** CPU, memory and disk over the last hour, 6 hours or 24 hours. Each chart is scaled to the machine's limit and refreshes live.
  - **Long lists:** worktrees, tasks, services, activity and logs show the newest entries, and "View all" opens a scrollable list.
  - **Phones:** on a phone, less-used actions move into a "More" menu.
- **Agent CLIs stay up to date between releases.** Every 6 hours the machine manager installs the newest Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Qwen Code that were published at least 48 hours ago.
  - **Who gets them:** every machine's agents and terminals use them from a shared read-only volume, so no agent can tamper with them.
  - **Safety:** an update never downgrades a CLI below the image's version, and each CLI must start before it's used.
  - **Settings:** `DEV_MACHINE_AGENT_CLI_REFRESH_HOURS` (0 turns it off) and `DEV_MACHINE_AGENT_CLI_MIN_AGE_HOURS`.
  - **Not covered:** Crush, Goose and Kimi still update with releases.

### Improvements
- **Complete usage history.** Machine usage now includes agent runs, checks and their services. It's kept for 24 hours and deleted when the machine is torn down.

### Fixed
- **`sudo apt-get update` on machines** couldn't reach the distribution mirrors. Machines now get both spellings of the proxy settings, and `sudo` keeps them. Existing machines get the fix the next time their terminal or IDE container is recreated, for example when they're started from stopped.

**v0.2.17 includes everything planned for v0.2.16**, whose image build failed a security scan, so it was never installable.

### Features
- **Read what a coding agent is doing.** A task's session now reads like a conversation instead of raw output. This applies in the new agent view and in the task card's "Execution output".
  - **Narration:** the agent's own messages are shown as text.
  - **Commands:** each one is a one-line step with its description and duration. It expands to the command and its output, long output is folded behind "Show N more lines", and failed commands are marked.
  - **Grouping:** runs of commands fold into "Ran N commands".
  - **Thinking:** shown as "Thought for Ns".
  - **Header:** a small header shows the model, the harness version and the working folder.
  - **Other content:** Claude Code and Codex sessions look the same, and unknown events fold into "N other events".
  - **Raw:** a toggle shows the original output.
- **Talk to an agent from the chat.** "Agent · ENG-1" in the conversation's top bar opens that task's agent thread in the middle of the assistant. With several tasks it's a menu with status dots.
  - **Breadcrumb:** "Assistant › ENG-1 · Iteration N" takes you back.
  - **Links:** the URL keeps the agent (`&agent=…`), so you can reload or share it.
  - **Replies:** while the agent view is open, the composer writes to that agent: live while it runs, otherwise at its next iteration.
  - **Questions:** each agent question has an "Answer the question" button right under it.
  - **Entry points:** "Open thread" in the chat and a task's row in Background tasks open the same view.
- **Self-hosted web search with SearXNG.** The assistant's web search can use your own SearXNG instance, with no API key and no per-query cost.
  - **Setup:** `selfhosting/searxng.sh enable` turns on the optional container and generates its secret key. Kuayle then offers "SearXNG (self-hosted)" in Settings → Assistant → Research.
  - **Security:** the SearXNG address is set by the server operator (`WEB_SEARCH_SEARXNG_URL`), never by a workspace. Only that host and port may be on a private network; every other private address is still refused, and redirects are never followed.
  - **Container:** off by default, reachable only from the backend on an internal network, read-only and unprivileged.

### Improvements
- **SearXNG errors:** if SearXNG isn't set to answer JSON, the assistant says exactly what to enable instead of failing silently.

### Fixed
- **CVE-2026-78661 (high, `golang.org/x/net/html`) in the images.**
  - **Rebuilt with x/net v0.62.0:** Caddy (web and all-in-one images), runc, the containerd shim, Docker Compose, Buildx and Crush in the dev machine images.
  - **Still affected:** dockerd, docker-proxy and rootlesskit in the upstream Docker image, because no Docker release has the fix yet. None of them parses HTML. The scan accepts exactly these versions until Docker ships a fix, and at the latest until 2026-12-31.

### Upgrade
- **Migration 116:** allows `searxng` as a web search provider.
- **No new GitHub App permissions.**
- **Optional:** run `selfhosting/searxng.sh enable` to use SearXNG, then choose it in Settings → Assistant → Research. Nothing changes until you do.

### Validation
- **Backend:** the full suite against PostgreSQL with all migrations applied, `go vet` and `govulncheck`. New tests cover:
  - the SearXNG provider: result mapping, caps and errors, including JSON being disabled;
  - the operator URL rules;
  - the allowed-host guard: the configured private host allowed, any other private address refused, redirects refused;
  - when settings offer or refuse SearXNG;
  - the self-hosting secret and update scripts.
- **UI:** `svelte-check`, unit tests (including the session parser: thinking, tool pairing, errors, oversized lines, Codex and unknown events) and the assistant, agent tasks, agent messages and research settings browser tests.
  - **New browser tests:** the agent view switch, deep links, the breadcrumb, the composer target, the answer button, the Raw toggle, live streaming, escaping and narrow screens.
- **Locally:** the agent view was tried against real test data before merging.
- **CI:** all result gates passed, and both PRs were reviewed by hand, security included.
